overview: Deckers Outdoor designs, markets and distributes footwear, apparel and accessories through a portfolio of premium consumer brands, led by HOKA (performance running/trail/hiking) and UGG (lifestyle footwear), plus a smaller Other Brands segment (primarily Teva). The company sells globally through wholesale partners and a growing direct-to-consumer network of e-commerce sites and ~200 company-owned retail stores, and manufactures almost entirely through independent contract factories in Vietnam and Indonesia. Fiscal year ends March 31; FY2026 net sales were $5.47 billion, up ~10% year-over-year.

business_model.summary: Deckers designs and markets footwear/apparel but outsources virtually all manufacturing to independent factories in Vietnam and Indonesia, generating revenue through wholesale distribution and an increasingly profitable direct-to-consumer (DTC) channel (e-commerce plus company-owned stores). HOKA and UGG together account for nearly all revenue and profit; growth is now driven mainly by DTC mix shift, international expansion (especially Asia), and product/category extensions (lifestyle, apparel) that reduce UGG's historical winter-boot seasonality.
business_model.customer_type: B2C via wholesale retail partners (department stores, specialty and sporting goods retailers, online marketplaces) and direct B2C via owned e-commerce (54 countries) and ~200 company-owned retail stores
business_model.geographic_mix: US ~55-60% of sales historically, with growing International contribution (EMEA and Asia-Pacific); Q1 FY2027 domestic net sales $517.4M vs international $502.1M, showing international now near parity and growing faster (+8.4% vs +3.2% domestic)

competitive_position.market_position: HOKA is a top-tier premium performance running/trail brand and a share gainer in specialty run retail over the past several years, though growth has decelerated sharply and On Running is now outgrowing it; UGG is the dominant premium sheepskin/lifestyle boot brand globally with near-monopoly-like brand recognition in that niche, now diversifying into year-round footwear (sneakers, Tasman) to reduce seasonality and fashion-cycle risk.

moat_factors.description: UGG has iconic, decades-long brand recognition; HOKA has built a strong reputation among runners for cushioned, technical performance footwear, supporting premium pricing
Growing owned e-commerce and retail footprint improves margins and customer data/relationships versus pure wholesale peers
Regular new launches (Clifton Pro, SpeedGoat 7) sustain HOKA's technical credibility; UGG line extensions (sneakers) reduce seasonality
Asset-light contract manufacturing avoids capital intensity but limits control and creates geographic concentration risk (Vietnam/Indonesia)
Footwear is a low-switching-cost category; loyalty is driven by brand/fashion preference rather than lock-in

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on two brands (HOKA and UGG) for nearly all revenue and profit; no meaningful third growth engine since Other Brands were divested/wound down
UGG remains exposed to fashion-cycle/fad risk despite diversification efforts, and its business is still seasonally weighted to Q3 (holiday boot season)
HOKA growth has decelerated materially (from 24-35% quarterly growth in FY2025 to high-single-digits in FY2026/Q1 FY2027) amid intensifying competition from On, Nike's running resurgence, and Adidas
Manufacturing concentration in Vietnam and Indonesia creates tariff and geopolitical/supply-chain exposure with limited near-term diversification
No meaningful international manufacturing or IP moat versus large, well-capitalized competitors (Nike, Adidas) that can outspend on marketing and R&D

growth_drivers: HOKA distribution expansion into additional sporting goods and specialty retail doors, expected to accelerate growth in H2 FY2027
UGG product diversification into year-round categories (sneakers, Tasman family) to reduce cold-weather/holiday seasonality and support higher full-price sell-through
International expansion, particularly Asia, where UGG and HOKA are seeing above-company-average growth rates
Continued DTC mix shift (e-commerce plus company-owned stores) which carries higher gross margins than wholesale
Potential tariff refunds from trade policy/legal challenges, which management says would be redeployed toward growth investment and shareholder returns
Large ongoing share buyback program ($1.075B repurchased in FY2026, ~$4.7B remaining authorization) supporting EPS growth even as revenue growth moderates

business.description: Quarterly HOKA growth has fallen from 24-35% in FY2025 to high-single-digits (7-8%) by Q1 FY2027 as On Running, Nike and Adidas intensify competition in performance running; a further slowdown would remove the company's primary growth engine
UGG's popularity has historically been cyclical; management and analysts flag that its current cycle of strength may be peaking, and consumer tastes in lifestyle footwear can shift quickly
HOKA and UGG together represent nearly all revenue; Other Brands (Teva) is immaterial after divesting Sanuk (Aug 2024) and phasing out Koolaburra/AHNU, leaving no diversified third leg
Well-capitalized competitors (Nike, Adidas, On, Skechers, Brooks) are investing heavily in running/lifestyle categories, pressuring HOKA's share gains and pricing power
No single wholesale customer exceeded 10% of FY2026 sales, but one customer represented 18.5% of trade receivables, creating collection concentration risk

financial.risk: Gross margin compression from tariffs and freight
financial.description: FY2026 tariffs reduced gross margin by ~80 bps; FY2027 guidance assumes a higher 12.5% effective tariff rate with no refunds assumed, pressuring margins further
$1.075B spent on repurchases in FY2026 and continued buybacks reduce balance-sheet cash cushion, though the company remains net-cash with ~$1.6-1.9B on hand

regulatory.description: Company paid ~$120M in tariffs in FY2026/early FY2027 tied to Vietnam/Indonesia sourcing; further escalation in US trade policy directly raises cost of goods with limited near-term ability to re-source manufacturing
Company is pursuing government refunds on tariffs paid but guidance assumes zero refund; a favorable or unfavorable resolution could swing margins

macro.description: Footwear/apparel purchases are discretionary; a US or global consumer slowdown would pressure both wholesale sell-in and DTC demand

Reliance on Vietnam and Indonesia for the vast majority of production exposes the company to regional disruptions (natural disasters, political instability, labor cost inflation, and further trade-policy shifts)
Growing international (Asia, EMEA) sales expose reported results to FX translation risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global athletic/lifestyle footwear market continues moderate growth, with premium performance running (HOKA's category) still expanding but now facing more intense multi-brand competition (Nike resurgence, On Running's rapid growth), while premium lifestyle/boot categories (UGG's category) are more fashion-cyclical and growing primarily through geographic and product-line diversification rather than core category expansion
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - both brands are consumer discretionary and UGG in particular carries seasonal (Q3-weighted) and fashion-cycle risk, though HOKA's more even quarterly distribution and international diversification are partially offsetting
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct exposure (net cash balance sheet, no meaningful long-term debt), moderate indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending and wholesale partner inventory financing
key_input_costs: Footwear materials (leather, synthetic uppers, foam/EVA midsoles)
Contract manufacturing labor costs in Vietnam/Indonesia

recent_developments.event: Q1 FY2027 results: record quarterly revenue of $1.02B (+5.7% YoY); HOKA +8% (some reports cite +7.7% to $703.5M), UGG +5% (some reports cite +4.9% to $278M); DTC net sales +13% vs wholesale +2.2%; management raised FY2027 EPS guidance to $7.35-$7.50 while maintaining revenue guidance of $5.86-$5.91B and raising the assumed effective tariff rate to 12.5%

Stock fell ~6% on the earnings print despite the beat and raised EPS guide, as investors focused on decelerating HOKA/UGG unit growth and tariff-driven margin pressure; shares have since fallen further, down roughly 30-34% from the 52-week high of $122.29 (set July 25, 2026)

Q4/full-year FY2026 results: net sales $5.472B (+9.8% YoY); HOKA net sales $2.587B (+15.9%); UGG net sales $2.739B (+8.2%); FY2026 gross margin guidance for FY2027 initially set near 56.5%, later nudged slightly better after Q1 outperformance
Board approved an additional $3.5B share repurchase authorization
Company repurchased ~10.5 million shares for ~$1.075B at a weighted average price of $102.43; remaining buyback authorization ~$4.7B as of June 30, 2026
Sanuk brand divested; Koolaburra and AHNU being phased out, concentrating the portfolio further into HOKA and UGG
Company paid roughly $120M in tariffs tied to Vietnam/Indonesia-sourced product; pursuing refunds through trade/legal channels with no refund assumed in guidance

items.notes: Implies ~7-8% YoY growth off FY2026's $5.472B base
Raised from prior guidance following stronger-than-expected Q1 results and continued share buybacks
Reflects ongoing tariff and freight cost headwinds offset by favorable DTC/product mix; assumes 12.5% effective tariff rate with no refunds
Raised from an earlier ~10% assumption; guidance assumes zero tariff refunds despite an active refund pursuit
Management flagged a YoY gross margin decline in Q2 specifically due to tariffs and rising freight costs, with HOKA distribution expansion expected to lift H2 growth

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Stefano Caroti highlighted new HOKA launches (Clifton Pro, SpeedGoat 7) resonating with consumers and planned expansion into additional sporting goods retail doors to accelerate H2 growth. Management emphasized UGG's product diversification (sneakers, Tasman family) as reducing cold-weather seasonality and supporting margin via mix, with particular strength in Asia. Management said any tariff refunds obtained would be redeployed toward growth investment and shareholder returns, and noted the company is supporting wholesale partners who absorbed some tariff costs. Capital allocation commentary emphasized continued buybacks (~$338M in the quarter) alongside a strong $1.6B+ cash position.

bull_case: HOKA remains a top-tier, share-gaining brand in performance running with a credible product pipeline (Clifton Pro, SpeedGoat 7) and untapped distribution expansion into sporting goods retail, offering a path back to double-digit growth

UGG's shift toward year-round product (sneakers, Tasman) and strong international/Asia growth reduce its historical seasonality and fashion-fad risk, extending its growth runway beyond the traditional winter boot cycle
DTC mix shift and international expansion structurally improve gross margins and diversify the revenue base away from US wholesale dependence
Aggressive capital return program (~$1.1B repurchased in FY2026, ~$4.7B authorization remaining) supports EPS growth and signals management confidence even amid a decelerating top line

Valuation has de-rated sharply (stock down ~30%+ from its 2026 high) while the company remains solidly profitable with a net-cash balance sheet, potentially pricing in more pessimism than fundamentals warrant if tariff and growth concerns prove transitory
bear_case: HOKA's growth has decelerated dramatically (from 24-35% to high-single-digits) as On Running, Nike and Adidas intensify competition, raising the risk that HOKA has entered a structurally slower growth phase rather than a temporary pause
UGG's popularity has always been cyclical and fashion-driven; current signs of deceleration could presage a more significant fad-driven downturn as has occurred in prior UGG cycles
Two-brand concentration (HOKA + UGG are essentially the entire business) leaves no diversified third growth engine after divesting Sanuk and winding down Koolaburra/AHNU
Tariff exposure is a persistent, rising cost headwind (effective rate assumption raised to 12.5%, ~$120M paid) with refund timing/outcome uncertain and guidance conservatively assuming zero refund

Heavy manufacturing concentration in Vietnam and Indonesia limits near-term ability to mitigate further trade-policy shocks or supply-chain disruptions, and consensus analyst sentiment (Hold rating, price targets being trimmed) reflects skepticism about the growth reacceleration story
